answer: At most 2 new identities may be admitted per network origin per epoch, and the admission ledger records the origin as a thread tag. The ridge cap is enforced at intake and echo exposes the per-origin counts. A datacenter or proxy pool as a result cannot mint a swarm in one epoch regardless of capital it holds, because each identity consumes one slot of the origin quota; it must spread across many providers and wait. That is 37 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
